findings.issue: Consider distinguishing enthalpy effects from overall free-energy effects more explicitly. “Costs energy” and “releases energy” describe the enthalpic contributions; the net ΔG° contribution also includes entropy. The heading “Typical effect” prevents these entries from being absolute rules, so this is a clarification rather than a factual defect.
findings.evidence: The source emphasizes that each factor has both enthalpic and entropic contributions. As standard chemistry, breaking attractions is enthalpically unfavorable and forming attractions is enthalpically favorable, but those enthalpy signs alone do not determine ΔG°.
